title: Sell Mineral Rights in Cowley, WY
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Cowley, WY | Big Horn County
metaDescription: Cowley, WY sits near the Elk Basin field on the Montana line in Big Horn County. Get an honest, courthouse-checked read on your mineral interest before selling.
heroLead: Cowley sits close to the Montana line, near the northern reach of the Elk Basin field, one of the oldest continuously developed oil fields in the Bighorn Basin.
intro: Elk Basin has been producing since 1915, straddling the state line, and its long life reflects decades of primary production followed by secondary and enhanced-recovery investment to keep pulling oil from formations that were first tapped over a hundred years ago. Big Horn County recorder records around Cowley reflect that history, with lease filings and probate transfers stacked across generations.

If your family's interest sits inside or near the Elk Basin boundary, there's real production history to check. If it sits further out, that's a different pricing conversation, and I'll tell you plainly which applies to your specific tract.

sections.heading: A field that crosses state lines
paragraphs: Because Elk Basin straddles Wyoming and Montana, unitization and royalty administration here can involve coordination across both states' regulatory frameworks. That adds a layer of complexity to title work that I account for before quoting anything, since I want your ownership confirmed cleanly on the Wyoming side specifically.

The field's continued enhanced-recovery investment after this many decades tells me there's still recoverable oil underneath a lot of this ground, which matters to how much runway a producing interest might still have.

sections.heading: Tracing multi-generation ownership
paragraphs: With production history this old, it's common for a Cowley-area interest to have passed through several estates since the original lease. I trace the Big Horn County recorder's index as far back as needed to confirm your exact fractional share before discussing any number.

I've handled Cowley-area title work where the original lessee company no longer exists under that name at all, absorbed through several mergers over the decades. Tracking down the current operator of record is part of the work I do before ever quoting you a figure.

faqs.question: Is Elk Basin still producing after over a century?
faqs.answer: Yes, portions remain active under enhanced recovery. I'll check the current status tied to your specific interest.

faqs.question: Does the field crossing into Montana complicate my Wyoming interest?
faqs.answer: It adds some complexity to unit administration, but I'll confirm your Wyoming-side ownership cleanly through Big Horn County records.

faqs.question: What if my mineral deed is from the 1920s or 30s?
faqs.answer: That's common in this part of the county. I can trace ownership through records that old without much trouble.

faqs.question: How do you find the current operator if the original company is gone?
faqs.answer: I trace lease assignments recorded at the courthouse to identify whoever currently administers the unit.
